name: Cantonese Beef in Black Bean Sauce
ingredients_verbatim: 1 medium brown onion, cut into 2.5cm squares
1 medium green capsicum, cut into 2.5cm squares
why: Verified in-band from the source page: 421 cal, 24g protein, 16g carbs per serving over 5, nutrition excludes rice. Structurally low-carb Cantonese stir-fry (sliced beef + capsicum + onion in a savory sauce, no rice/pasta/potato/bean base). Stir-fry style beef fits the beef-skillet lane and scales to 14 by weigh-and-divide in a wok/large skillet. Genuine cuisine gap: the catalog's Chinese beef entries are honey-black-pepper, mushroom stir-fry, chow mein and bulgogi - none is black-bean-sauce beef, and it is not in the current candidate pool. Two signature ingredients have NO board home - Chinese preserved/fermented black beans (douchi, distinct from canned-black-beans) and Shaoxing cooking wine - flagged as a deliberate pricer-lane test, not filtered out. Beef rump maps to sirloin-steak. Confidence high on the numbers (read from the recipe card); the one caveat is cal 421 sits near the 400 floor, so label-DB macros could drift slightly under - the fatty stir-fry oil makes a real sub-400 drop unlikely.
